newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil "check tax" to take effect Jan 23.
newsitem.headline: Brazil "check tax" to take effect Jan 23.

text.p: Brazil will introduce a 0.2 percent tax on financial transactions on January 23 following publication Friday in the government's Official Journal of the bill setting up the levy, officials said.
The so-called CPMF check tax is designed to raise about 400 million reais a month to help fund the health services.
A constitutional amendment allowing the tax to be levied and a bill setting up the regulatory framework were passed by Congress.
The tax takes effect for a year but a clause in the regulatory bill allows for it to be continued for another year.
Government bodies, including the federal government, the states and cities and state-owned firms, will be exempt.
Transfers between accounts belonging to the same person or firm are also exempt, as are financial transactions by institutions on behalf of third parties, a measure intended to avoid double-taxation.
Those earning less than three minimum salaries a month, currently 336 reais, and state pensioners will be compensated.
